Hi Marissa / Jonas,

Thanks for the demo earlier — that was helpful. Per our internal discussion I wanted to capture the numbers we care most about so you can recommend the best deployment mode (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private). High level: this will be a customer-facing feature (help center summarization + short answers) and latency matters.

Quick facts from our side:
- Traffic profile: baseline 30 QPS, typical working hours spike to 80 QPS, marketing events could push short bursts to ~200 QPS for 10–20 minutes.
- Latency targets: p95 <= 120 ms, p99 ideally < 300 ms for 512-token responses.
- Payloads: average generation length ~250 tokens, occasionally up to 1k tokens.
- Data: no PHI, but logs must be retained for 90 days for analytics; we need SOC2 evidence.

We like the simplicity of Hosted but worried about P99 stability in heavy bursts. If Dedicated is the recommendation, what lead time and commitment are typical? Also looped in procurement for any questions on terms.

Sanjay — thanks for the clear numbers and for looping procurement. Quick post-call recap and proposed next steps below. I also attached a short worksheet (deployment_requirements.xlsx) so your infra folks can fill exact SLAs/traffic windows if helpful.

Recap of requirements from call:
- Primary objective: customer-facing generation with P95 target <= 120ms, P99 target < 300ms for 512-token responses.
- Traffic: baseline 30 QPS, expected steady 80 QPS during business hours, short burst capacity ~200 QPS (10–20 minutes).
- Data retention: 90 days, SOC 2 evidence required.
- Preference: Hosted for speed to production, Dedicated if Hosted cannot guarantee p99 stability for bursts.

Decision considerations (short):
- Hosted API: fastest to value, no infra commit. Can autoscale but p99 under bursty traffic depends on available pooled capacity and routing policies; we can provide regional pinning and priority routing for critical traffic to improve stability.
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pool for predictable throughput and stable P99 at scale; recommended if you want hard guarantees for sustained bursts without cold-start variability.
- Private/VPC: recommended only if you have regulatory constraints or require on-prem control; higher ops/lead time.

Ask from your side: can your infra/ops team confirm whether the 200 QPS burst is single-region or can be shifted across regions? That matters for routing and headroom planning.

Proposed next steps:
1) Your team completes deployment_requirements.xlsx and returns with any additional burst schedule details (Jonas will help translate to capacity estimates).
2) We run a hosted stress test against a small synthetic workload to validate p95/p99 for 512-token responses. If hosted looks marginal, we’ll size a Dedicated trial (2–4 week reserved pool) and share cost/lead-time.
3) Procurement and legal to review the attached starter SOW/proposal.

I’ve attached: deployment_requirements.xlsx and a one-pager on Dedicated capacity (redwood-dedicated-capacity-cheatsheet.pdf). Dev / Jonas — can you draft the stress test plan and an estimated Dedicated sizing based on the numbers above?

Sanjay — thanks for the worksheet and the regional detail — that makes sizing straightforward. Quick technical readout and proposal: 

Technical summary based on your numbers (512-token gen):
- Baseline 30 QPS: Hosted will easily meet p95/p99 under normal conditions.
- Steady 80 QPS: Hosted should still be fine most of the time but p99 headroom during concurrent multi-tenant bursts is the risk.
- Short single-region bursts to 200 QPS: Dedicated is the safer option if you need firm P99 guarantees at those burst levels, especially for customer-facing traffic where SLA slippage is visible.

Recommended approach (pragmatic, low friction):
1) Hosted proof-of-behavior (2 weeks): we run a hosted stress test in us-west using production-weighted traffic (we'll simulate your event burst schedule). Goal: validate p95/p99 for 512-token responses and measure token cost. If p99 <= 300ms for burst windows, you can stay on Hosted with a priority routing knob and rate-based reservation for predictable capacity.
2) Dedicated trial (2–4 weeks) if hosted fails the p99 goal: we provision a small Dedicated pool sized to sustain 200 QPS at target latency. We estimate required baseline pool: 4x A100-equivalent GPUs (approx), trial cost and exact sizing in the attached proposal (proposal_RWD-LEX-2026-0012.pdf).
3) Operational items: SOC2 evidence and 90-day retention are standard; we'll provide the audit pack and update our data retention policy in the contract.

Next steps:
- Marissa: can you confirm the trial window procurement is asking for (30 days) — we can do a hosted proofof-behavior within that window.
- Sanjay: share any hard event dates so we can schedule the simulated bursts.

Jonas: I’ll follow up with a precise loadscript and estimated Dedicated sizing by EOD.

Thanks,
